title: China's Z.ai disables AI coding assistant features after security issue

reading.body:
This is a data handling failure in a developer tool, not a model error. A coding assistant that runs inside a local development environment sent local code repositories to a cloud provider, and the route that did so was a Codebase Indexing feature that shipped enabled by default. The failure sits in the deployment configuration rather than in the model's output: nothing the assistant generated was wrong, but code the developers had not agreed to share left their machines.

Catching it would have required the upload path to be off unless a user turned it on, and a clear statement at setup of what leaves the local environment and where it goes. A default-on setting that transmits source code is the kind of behaviour that only surfaces when someone inspects outbound traffic or reads the configuration closely, which is what the developers here appear to have done.

Z.ai apologised, fixed the vulnerability and later disabled the upload route, and said independent reviews found no code data was retained. That last point is the company's own account and is not established by the reporting. One company withdrew a separate claim that six workspaces with sensitive data had been sent, so that allegation does not stand as a finding either.

reports.title: China's Z.ai disables AI coding assistant features after security issue

summary: Developers said Z.ai's ZCode AI coding assistant sent local code repositories to Alibaba Cloud without their agreement. Z.ai blamed a Codebase Indexing feature that was on by default. The company apologized, fixed the vulnerability, and later turned off the upload route. One company withdrew a separate claim that six workspaces with sensitive data had been sent. Z.ai said independent reviews found no code data was kept.
title_en: China's Z.ai disables AI coding assistant features after security issue
